drc.description: Run the stock KLayout DRC deck of the PDK on a layout and give a typed verdict. Inputs: gds (the layout, relative to the design root), cell (the top cell), rule_set (optional; a rule set of the technology pack, for example main or full; the default is the default set of the pack), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK), max_examples (optional, default 8). The adapter reconciles the verdict with the exit code of the deck and the marker database: the counts are measured only when the deck wrote a complete marker database and its exit code agrees with the marker count. Else the run is 'not run': markers and rules_violated are failed, the response is failed, and an error diagnostic gives the reason and the last lines of the deck log. A printed summary without a complete report is not a result. Measurements: markers (all markers), rules_violated (the number of rules with markers), runtime_s. Diagnostics: one error per violated rule, largest count first, with the rule name, the count, the rule description of the deck and the first max_examples marker boxes in µm (cell coordinates), grouped by cell. When a rule has more markers, the error gives the marker count of each cell and the number of the other boxes. The last diagnostic gives the paths of work/drc.json (the full table: each rule with its description, count, cells and all boxes) and of the marker database. The outputs have the marker database and the deck log. Use it instead of a DRC shell script, so that each run is recorded.

lvs.description: Run the stock KLayout LVS deck of the PDK: compare a layout with a reference netlist, and give a typed verdict. Inputs: gds, cell (the top cell), netlist (the reference netlist, relative to the design root, in the netlist form of the pack), pins (optional; the pins of the top cell in order), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK). A match is given only from a complete LVS database: the deck log has the match text of the pack, the exit code is a code of a completed run, the LVS database exists and loads in KLayout, and its compare status is a match. Else the result is 'not run' (all counts failed, the response failed), with an error diagnostic that names the condition that failed. A printed match from a run that crashed or left a truncated database is not a match. Measurements: match (1 or 0), unmatched_devices, unmatched_nets, unmatched_pins (the pins of the input pins that are not pins of the extracted top circuit or of the reference circuit, or are in a different order than in the reference netlist; the extracted circuit sorts its pins by name, so the order is the order of the reference netlist), runtime_s. On a mismatch, error diagnostics give the circuits, devices and nets that do not match (up to 10 each); work/lvs.json has all of them and the pin check. Each pin problem is a warning, also on a match. The outputs have the extracted netlist, the LVS database and the deck log. Use it instead of an LVS shell script, so that each run is recorded.

query.description: Answer questions about a layout in one run, without a deck and without Python. Inputs: gds (the layout, relative to the design root), cell (the top cell), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK), queries (a list of questions; each is an object with a kind and its arguments). Boxes and points are in µm, in top-cell coordinates: box is [x1, y1, x2, y2] or a point [x, y]. A layer is a name of the layer properties file of the PDK (Metal1 or Metal1.drawing, met1) or layer/datatype (8/0). The kinds: layers (each layer with its name, layer/datatype, flat shape count and area in µm²); cells (the cell tree with flat instance count, bbox and own-shape count; depth, default 2, limits the listing); shapes (layer, box, max default 20: the flat shapes that touch the box, largest overlap first, each with its cell path, plus the total count and the merged area in the box); instances (box, max default 20: each instance that touches the box, with its cell, cell path, placement in the top cell and bbox); at (box: per layer the shape count and merged area in the box, the deepest instances that touch it and the texts in it); bbox (optional layer, optional cell); texts (optional layer, optional box); distance (layer, box_a, box_b: the smallest distance between the shapes in the two boxes, with the two closest edges). The answers are rows in the report of the result: one header line per question, '[i] <kind> ...', then the rows, indented. The rows are short and fixed: µm with 3 decimals, boxes as (x1,y1;x2,y2), points as (x,y), placements as (x,y) r<angle> [mx]. The report has at most 200 lines; work/query.json has the full answer of each question. A bad question gives an error diagnostic for that question, and the other questions are still answered; the run is completed when at least one question was answered. Measurements: queries, rows, runtime_s. Use it to read a layout: put several questions in one call, for example at on a DRC marker box, then shapes and distance near it, instead of a Python script.

diff.description: Compare two layouts in one run, and optionally the DRC markers of two runs, without a deck and without Python. Inputs: gds (the new layout, relative to the design root), against (the old layout: a path relative to the design root, or git:<ref> or git:<ref>:<path>; the adapter writes the file of the ref to work/against.gds with git show and records the command), cell (the top cell; the same name in both files), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK), layers (optional; a list of layer names or layer/datatype; the default is all layers of both files), box (optional; [x1, y1, x2, y2] in µm: compare only in this box), max (optional, default 10: the polygons shown per layer and direction, and the markers shown per rule and direction), drc and drc_against (optional, together: the ids of two completed klayout drc experiments, of gds and of against). The layers: an XOR of the merged shapes of each layer, for the whole tree of the top cell (in the deep mode of KLayout when no box is given). Per changed layer, one row with the area added and removed in µm² and the polygon counts, then the largest polygons first, each with its bbox, area and the cell path of the instance that holds it (the top cell when it is not inside one instance). '+' is in gds and not in against; '-' is in against and not in gds. The layers with no difference are counted in one row. The cells: the cells only in one file, the cells whose flat instance count differs, the cells whose child instances differ (added, removed or moved placements), and, when the hierarchy is the same, the cells whose own shapes differ. The DRC markers: per rule the new, fixed and unchanged markers; a marker is unchanged when the other run has a marker of the same cell with the same box within one database unit. The report has at most 200 lines; work/diff.json has the full answer. Measurements: layers_changed, area_added_um2, area_removed_um2, cells_changed, markers_new, markers_fixed, markers_unchanged (missing without drc and drc_against; failed when they are given but cannot be read), runtime_s. Input files: both layouts (role layout), the layer properties file, the pack and the two marker tables (role drc). Use it to see what an edit or a commit changed, instead of a Python script.

render.description: Draw a region of a layout, or a DRC marker, as a PNG picture in one run, without a deck and without Python. The picture comes with the result (an image part after the summary). Inputs: gds (the layout, relative to the design root), cell (the top cell), technology (optional; the default is the pack for $PDK), and one view: box ([x1, y1, x2, y2] in µm, in top-cell coordinates; a point [x, y] gives a view of 1 µm) or drc (the id of a completed klayout drc experiment) with rule (the rule name as the drc report gives it): the marker of that rule is drawn as a red outline, with at least 3 µm around it; index (default 1) chooses the marker, in the order of the drc table; all true draws one picture per marker, up to max (default 4, at most 8). Options: layers (a list of layer names of the layer properties file of the PDK, or layer/datatype; the default is all layers), size (the longer side in pixels, default 1024, at most 2048), labels (show texts, default true), grid (show the scale bar, and a 1 µm grid for a view up to 50 µm, default true), hierarchy (the levels of cells to draw: 0 is the top cell alone; the default is all). The colours are the colours of the layer properties file of the PDK. The view is the box plus a margin of 10 % (at least 0.5 µm). The report has one line per picture: the box, the view box, the file (work/render.png, or work/render-<n>.png) and the layers with shapes in the view; work/render.json has the full answer. Measurements: images, runtime_s. Use it to look at a marker or a region before you choose the edit, instead of reasoning from coordinates alone.
